summary: Student-first machine candidate based on Jagiellonian Rector Ordinance No. 115/2025. It covers teaching activities, coursework, and theses only as stated in that ordinance; no separate exam or data rule is inferred.

dimensions.summary: The ordinance permits AI-based tools in teaching activities while requiring transparent course rules from teaching staff. Scope: ordinance-defined teaching activities.

do: Check the transparent AI rule given for your course.
dont: Do not assume the general ordinance replaces the instructor course rule.

dimensions.summary: No source-backed exam-specific rule is included; this is not evidence of permission or prohibition.
Students must clearly mark AI-generated parts of coursework, theses, or other assignments. Scope: the cited Rector Ordinance.

do: Mark the parts of your work generated with AI-based tools.
dont: Do not submit AI-generated parts without the required marking.

dimensions.summary: No source-backed student data-entry rule is included; this is not evidence of permission or prohibition.
The ordinance permits use of AI-based tools in teaching activities but does not make a general course or assessment permission decision for every tool.

do: Check the course rule for the particular tool and task.
dont: Do not read “AI-based tools” as a blanket assessment approval.

dimensions.summary: The cited ordinance expressly includes theses among work whose AI-generated parts must be clearly marked. Scope: that ordinance, not a separate journal policy.

do: Check the ordinance before using AI in thesis work and mark generated parts.
dont: Do not generalize this to external publication rules without checking the publisher.
